message.content: {"answer":[{"text":"The device can use a trained deep learning model on measurable 4G/5G KPIs, time, and location to predict whether an NR RACH attempt is likely to fail, and then avoid triggering the NR RACH procedure when failure is likely.","evidence_ids":[2]},{"text":"It can also stop NR measurement operations after detecting a continuous NR RACH failure situation, which prevents later link attempts that would trigger more failures.","evidence_ids":[2]},{"text":"To select connectivity for best throughput, the device can compare predicted downlink throughput for LTE-only mode versus EN-DC mode and enable or maintain EN-DC only when its inferred throughput is higher.","evidence_ids":[9]},{"text":"If the inferred EN-DC throughput is lower than LTE-only throughput, the device should keep or switch to LTE-only mode instead of enabling EN-DC.","evidence_ids":[9]}]}

{"answer":[{"text":"Prevention should prioritize the pesticide classes with the clearest elevated breast-cancer risks in farm households, especially organophosphates, because the study found increased risk for chlorpyrifos, terbufos, and fonofos, with some evidence also for coumaphos and heptachlor.","evidence_ids":[7]},{"text":"Within organophosphates, the findings suggest focusing on women’s direct exposure to chlorpyrifos and terbufos, since these were associated with elevated risk in the wives’ analyses.","evidence_ids":[7]},{"text":"Prevention should also consider indirect household exposure from husbands’ pesticide use, because husbands’ use of 2,4,5-TP was associated with elevated breast-cancer risk and terbufos showed elevated risk in both spouses’ use analyses.","evidence_ids":[7,8]},{"text":"The evidence suggests that risk may be greater among premenopausal women for some pesticides, so prevention efforts may need to pay special attention to younger or premenopausal farm households.","evidence_ids":[7,8]},{"text":"Because the studies found little consistent association for many other pesticide classes, prevention priorities should be more targeted than broad, class-wide for all pesticides.","evidence_ids":[7,8]}]}

{"answer":[{"text":"Applying exact gradient updates can make the probabilistic policy converge to an optimal solution only very slowly, so the tradeoff is between exactness and convergence speed.","evidence_ids":[5]},{"text":"In the cited example, the exact gradient method improved the policy but the convergence was described as severe non-linearity and slow, while annealing or taking the most probable action converged faster.","evidence_ids":[5]},{"text":"Thus, exact gradient updates on induced finite-state models trade faster practical progress for a more global, exact policy improvement step.","evidence_ids":[5]}]}

{"answer":[{"text":"In FINEARTS-HF, the early composite benefit of finerenone was mainly driven by fewer heart-failure hospitalizations, while the cardiovascular-death component became more influential later in follow-up. [8]","evidence_ids":[8]},{"text":"The hierarchical composite win ratio was already above 1.0 by 60 days and then plateaued after about 12 months, suggesting that early composite benefits did predict broader pooled-event reductions over time. [8]","evidence_ids":[8]},{"text":"Across the pooled FINE-HEART analysis, finerenone reduced cardiovascular death or heart-failure hospitalization overall, and the effect was consistent across the contributing trials and key subgroups. [9]","evidence_ids":[9]},{"text":"The pooled analysis therefore supports that trial-specific early composite benefits can generalize to broader pooled-event reductions, although the magnitude was modest and not all individual components were significantly reduced. [8,9]","evidence_ids":[8,9]}]}

{"answer":[{"text":"In systemic sclerosis-associated interstitial lung disease, worsening lung function over 12 months predicted higher mortality, but digital ulcer burden alone did not. [8]","evidence_ids":[8]},{"text":"The study found that a decline in FVC >10% predicted was associated with decreased survival, and composite measures combining FVC decline with DLCO decline or worsening mRSS also predicted mortality. [8]","evidence_ids":[8]},{"text":"A separate systemic sclerosis digital-ulcer guideline states that digital ulcers are associated with a worse prognosis and death in systemic sclerosis, but it does not provide evidence that healing fingertip ischemic lesions improves long-term survival. [9]","evidence_ids":[9]}]}

{"answer":[{"text":"Combining surfactant-rich fluids with acid-sensitive porous carriers can improve apparent solubility and bioaccessibility by letting micelles take up material released from the carrier. [3,6]","evidence_ids":[3,6]},{"text":"The tradeoff is that acidic conditions can destabilize or disintegrate the porous carrier, which may release the payload in an insoluble or less useful form. [3,6]","evidence_ids":[3,6]},{"text":"In the cited examples, Tween 80 helped retain and solubilize curcumin, while bile salts could compete with or displace curcumin from the carrier and reduce apparent solubility in some settings. [3,6]","evidence_ids":[3,6]},{"text":"Thus, the benefit of surfactant-assisted uptake comes with the risk that acid-sensitive carriers lose structural integrity under acidic conditions, limiting controlled release. [3,6]","evidence_ids":[3,6]}]}

{"answer":[{"text":"The prior-treatment feature most clearly linked to better survival benefit from the newer second-line option is a longer duration of prior gemcitabine plus nab-paclitaxel (GnP) treatment, with ≥7.2 months associated with longer OS on NFF than <7.2 months. [4]","evidence_ids":[4]},{"text":"In contrast, prior exposure to irinotecan, fluorouracil, or platinum did not identify a survival-benefit subgroup because OS was similar between users and non-users of each prior therapy. {"answer":[{"text":"Hands-on projects can be used to create real, contextual problem-solving tasks that require students to analyze, design, test, and evaluate solutions, which supports critical thinking in physics. [8, 9]","evidence_ids":[8,9]},{"text":"Simulations can complement projects by making abstract physics concepts more tangible and by helping students visualize and test ideas during learning. [9, 8]","evidence_ids":[9,8]},{"text":"A combined approach is supported by evidence that project-based STEAM learning with visual simulations improved critical thinking more than conventional instruction in optics. [9]","evidence_ids":[9]},{"text":"Another study found that a STEAM-integrated SSCS model with miniature product creation improved critical thinking more than conventional learning in static fluid topics. [8]","evidence_ids":[8]},{"text":"Together, the evidence suggests that combining hands-on projects with simulations can maximize physics critical thinking by linking active experimentation with clearer conceptual understanding. [8, 9]","evidence_ids":[8,9]}]}

{"answer":[{"text":"Language barriers can delay or hinder timely access to emergency care because patients may struggle to communicate symptoms, needs, or requests for help, and may need family members or interpreters to translate. [3,5]","evidence_ids":[3,5]},{"text":"Low health literacy can make it harder for people to understand how the health system works, what services they can access, and what to expect, which can lead to missed or delayed care. [3,5]","evidence_ids":[3,5]},{"text":"Communication problems can also reduce trust and make care feel less safe or less compassionate, which may further discourage people from seeking or continuing emergency care. [3,5]","evidence_ids":[3,5]},{"text":"The evidence also notes that providing reliable information in multiple languages and offering professional interpreters are important ways to improve equitable access and outcomes. [3,5]","evidence_ids":[3,5]}]}

{"answer":[{"text":"In PrVO4, the transition pressure drops when hydrostaticity decreases, because nonhydrostatic conditions alter the structural sequence and can favor different high-pressure phases. [5]","evidence_ids":[5]},{"text":"In minrecordite, deviatoric stress from less hydrostatic media lowers the phase-transition onset, with the transition occurring at 13.4(3) GPa in Ne, 10.7(4) GPa in silicone oil, and at even lower pressure without a pressure-transmitting medium. [8]","evidence_ids":[8]},{"text":"The minrecordite study also concludes that higher Zn substitution for Mg lowers the transition pressure in dolomite-type carbonates, with the onset decreasing when the Zn/Mg ratio exceeds 1. [8]","evidence_ids":[8]},{"text":"Together, these documents support that stress anisotropy or deviatoric stress and cation substitution both reduce transition pressures by changing the relative stability and kinetics of competing structures. [5,8]","evidence_ids":[5,8]}]}

{"answer":[{"text":"Real-time self-monitoring can provide high-resolution, repeated measures that help clinicians see symptom patterns outside face-to-face visits and use them to inform care decisions.","evidence_ids":[3,5]},{"text":"When monitored data show substantial improvement, the information can help adjust the scheduling and frequency of face-to-face sessions and support triage decisions.","evidence_ids":[3]},{"text":"In anxiety care, combining passive signals from smartphones or wearables with self-reported data is described as a way to support the patient journey from screening and diagnosis through monitoring and treatment.","evidence_ids":[1,5]},{"text":"In depression research, mobile phone behavioral markers and intermittent self-reports are described as useful for supplementing clinical evaluations and monitoring relapse over time.","evidence_ids":[1,5]},{"text":"In suicide research, ecological momentary assessment data combined with AI has shown promise for predicting near-term suicidal ideation, which could support risk-sensitive thresholds.","evidence_ids":[5,7]}]}

{"answer":[{"text":"Yes; the wellness-course study found that participants improved in spirituality, mindfulness, depressed mood, psychological flexibility, and anxiety after attending holistic programs compared with vacation controls, suggesting some people benefit more than others depending on the course and their baseline characteristics.","evidence_ids":[8]},{"text":"The study also noted that participants entered the courses for different reasons, including physical, emotional, mental health, or spiritual concerns, which implies that individualized profiles could help match people to the most relevant retreat format.","evidence_ids":[8]},{"text":"Another Ayurvedic study reported that different imbalance profiles were associated with different psychological patterns, and it concluded that diagnostic assessment may help inform personalized treatment, supporting the broader idea that individualized profiles can guide who benefits most from a holistic approach.","evidence_ids":[9]}]}

{"answer":[{"text":"Improving institutional care readiness may not lower mortality equally across regions because the underlying mortality burden is geographically clustered and varies by area, so some regions still have higher-risk hotspots even when services improve. [3]","evidence_ids":[3]},{"text":"The effect of readiness also differs by local context: in Ethiopia, higher mortality was linked to rural residence, younger maternal age, higher birth rates, low autonomy, and anemia, which means facility improvements alone may not offset these region-specific drivers. [3]","evidence_ids":[3]},{"text":"The evidence on respectful maternity care also shows that institutional readiness is uneven across regions, with urban regions, higher proportions of trained providers, and maternity waiting homes associated with better readiness, while agrarian and pastoralist areas had weaker support mechanisms. [2]","evidence_ids":[2]},{"text":"Because of these regional differences in resources, supervision, and community access, strengthening care readiness can improve outcomes overall but still leave unequal mortality reductions across regions. [2,3]","evidence_ids":[2,3]}]}

{"answer":[{"text":"Hit-grouping window instability can be mitigated by increasing the slicer time window so slow tracks still accumulate enough hits to be grouped, with 25 µs reported as a good setting for preserving efficiency at lower β while keeping higher-β performance acceptable.","evidence_ids":[8,9]},{"text":"The evidence also suggests keeping the ADC cut at 100 for the 25 µs window when aiming to preserve sensitivity to very slow events, because this combination improved low-β detection without negative effects for the higher-speed monopoles studied.","evidence_ids":[8,9]},{"text":"If even slower events must be retained, the window can be pushed to 50 µs, but the evidence says the slicer breaks above 50 µs and that this requires additional changes such as raising the slice sum ADC max cut.","evidence_ids":[8,9]}]}

{"answer":[{"text":"The case-based learning studies at SMAN 4 Pariaman and SMAN 1 Pariangan both report higher posttest scores in the experimental class than in the control class, indicating positive learning gains from the case-focused approach.","evidence_ids":[4,9]},{"text":"At SMAN 4 Pariaman, the experimental class rose from a pretest mean of 54.87 to a posttest mean of 83.53, while the control class rose from 58.65 to 76.93.","evidence_ids":[4]},{"text":"At SMAN 1 Pariangan, the experimental class rose from a pretest mean of 51.17 to a posttest mean of 82.77, while the control class rose from 49.29 to 69.97.","evidence_ids":[9]},{"text":"Both studies report statistically significant differences for the case-based learning intervention, with p-values of 0.001 at SMAN 4 Pariaman and 0.000 at SMAN 1 Pariangan.","evidence_ids":[4,9]},{"text":"The gains appear consistent across the two high schools, but the experimental class improvement is larger than the control class improvement in both studies.","evidence_ids":[4,9]}]}

{"answer":[{"text":"Yes; in anti–PD-1–resistant melanoma, intratumoral BO-112 plus pembrolizumab produced a 25% objective response rate and met its primary endpoint, suggesting intratumoral immune priming can help overcome resistance.","evidence_ids":[6]},{"text":"The trial included patients whose anti–PD-1 therapy had been given in the adjuvant setting and who then progressed, so the evidence directly includes relapse after adjuvant anti–PD-1 therapy.","evidence_ids":[6]},{"text":"Responses were seen in both injected and noninjected lesions, which is consistent with a broader immune-priming effect beyond the injected tumor sites.","evidence_ids":[6]},{"text":"The combination was generally well tolerated, with 38.1% grade 3-5 adverse events and 9.5% considered drug-related.","evidence_ids":[6]}]}
